ownership_reason: Only the gold decides, for each timestamp, whether it is written into the local file data and what the flags byte says: hop 1 reads the flags byte as unsigned, hops 2 and 4 pass the flags and the timestamps along, and hop 3 makes room for every timestamp and returns exactly the count of bytes the gold reports. The gold's javadoc promises the local file data layout of the extended timestamp extra field, in which the flags byte tells which timestamps are present in the data (X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.setFlags/getFlags documentation); on the trigger input (three timestamps set, then setFlags(1)) the variant writes the flags byte 1 followed by three timestamps. The convention is pinned outside the gold by the intact siblings X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.getLocalFileDataLength (counts a timestamp only when its bit is set), parseFromLocalFileData (reads only the timestamps whose bits are set) and toString (shows a timestamp only when its bit is set), and by passing tests: testGettersSetters (all three times set, flags 1, 2 and 4 each give a local length of 5), testWriteReadRoundtrip and testSampleFile (local data through the chain), testBitsAreSetWithTime.
